The matrix is upper triangular, so the determinant is the product of the diagonal entries. Therefore \(\\det=1\)*\(3\cdot5\) = 15.

Column 3 is \((0,0,6)\), so only the entry 6 contributes. Its sign in position \((3,3)\) is positive. The minor is \(\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\4&3\end{pmatrix}\), whose determinant is \(2\cdot3\) - \(1\cdot4\) = 2. Therefore \(\\det=6\)*2 = 12.

questions.prompt: Use a row operation to compute \(\det\left(\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\3&8\end{pmatrix}\right)\).
questions.answer: Use \(\mathbb R^2\) <- \(\mathbb R^2\) - 3R1, which does not change the determinant. The matrix becomes \(\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&2\end{pmatrix}\). This triangular matrix has determinant \(1\cdot2\) = 2. Therefore the original determinant is 2.
Use ad - bc: \(\\det=2\)*2 - \(4\cdot1\) = 4 - 4 = 0. A zero determinant means the rows and columns are linearly dependent, and the matrix is not invertible.

Expand along row 1: \(\\det=1\)*\(\det\left(\begin{pmatrix}3&4\\1&2\end{pmatrix}\right)\) - \(1\cdot \det\left(\begin{pmatrix}2&4\\0&2\end{pmatrix}\right)\) + \(1\cdot \det\left(\begin{pmatrix}2&3\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\right)\). The minors are \(3\cdot2\) - \(4\cdot1\) = 2, \(2\cdot2\) - \(4\cdot0\) = 4, and \(2\cdot1\) - \(3\cdot0\) = 2. Therefore \(\\det=2\) - 4 + 2 = 0.

Row 1 is \((0,2,0)\), so only the middle entry contributes. Its sign is negative in position \((1,2)\). The minor is \(\begin{pmatrix}1&4\\5&7\end{pmatrix}\), with determinant \(1\cdot7\) - \(4\cdot5\) = 7 - 20 = -13. Therefore \(\\det=-2\)*(-13) = 26.

questions.prompt: Compute \(\det\left(\begin{pmatrix}2&1&3\\0&4&5\\0&2&1\end{pmatrix}\right)\) by first expanding along column 1.
questions.answer: Column 1 is \((2,0,0)\), so only the first entry contributes. Its sign is positive. The minor is \(\begin{pmatrix}4&5\\2&1\end{pmatrix}\), whose determinant is \(4\cdot1\) - \(5\cdot2\) = 4 - 10 = -6. Therefore \(\\det=2\)*(-6) = -12.

Use determinant-preserving operations. Apply \(\mathbb R^2\) <- \(\mathbb R^2\) - 2R1 to get \(\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\0&3&1\\0&3&2\end{pmatrix}\). Then apply \(\mathbb R^3\) <- \(\mathbb R^3\) - \(\mathbb R^2\) to get \(\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\0&3&1\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}\). The matrix is triangular, so the determinant is \(2\cdot3\)*1 = 6. The row replacement operations did not change the determinant, so the original determinant is 6.

questions.prompt: Find all real t such that \(\det\left(\begin{pmatrix}t&2\\8&t\end{pmatrix}\right)\) = 0.
questions.answer: Compute the determinant: t*t - \(2\cdot8\) = \(t^2\) - 16. Set it equal to zero: \(t^2\) - 16 = 0. Factor: (t - 4)(t + 4) = 0. Therefore \(t=4\) or \(t=-4\).
